pins.title: Sauna Blanket or Home Sauna? Answer These 2 Questions Before You Buy
pins.subtitle: Space and how you like to relax
pins.description: Two questions settle the sauna blanket vs home sauna decision: do you have a permanent 3x3 ft space to dedicate, and would you rather sit upright than lie down for a session? Two yeses point to a standalone sauna. Otherwise, a blanket is the lower-risk way to see if a sweat routine sticks. #saunablanket #homesauna #infraredsauna #homewellness #recoveryroutine #smallspaceliving

pins.title: Infrared Sauna Blanket for Small Apartments: Why It Fits Renters Better Than a Sauna
pins.subtitle: Stores flat, no permanent footprint
pins.description: Renting or short on space? A zip-up infrared sauna blanket heats you directly, stores flat in a closet, and needs no assembly or electrical work. The tradeoff: you lie down zipped in, so you can't read or work during a session. Full side-by-side with standalone home saunas on price tier, space, setup, and heat style. #saunablanket #apartmentliving #renterfriendly #infraredsauna #smallspaces #homewellness

pins.title: When Is a Home Sauna Worth It Over a Sauna Blanket? A Practical Comparison
pins.subtitle: Price tier, space, setup, heat style
pins.description: A standalone home sauna makes sense if you have the space and know you will use it several times a week for the long haul. You can sit, read, and decompress in a way a blanket doesn't allow, but it needs a dedicated footprint and sometimes electrical work. Compare both options before committing. #homesauna #saunablanket #recoveryroutine #homewellness #selfcareathome #infraredsauna
